doc: Scene manifest for game-show-v1. Everything the Rust app needs that a GLB cannot carry,
and the single source of truth for every material value the renderer applies.
REGENERATED in the cleanup pass of 2026-07-30 from two ground truths and nothing else:
a read-only `blender --background wheel_stage.blend --python <dump>` run, and a parse of
assets/wheel_stage.glb. The .blend was never saved. No look-dev value survives in this
file: every material field below is what the .blend holds.
TO REGENERATE: run blender --background <blend> --python <dump> and read the scene, the
world, Cam_Hero, the six lights, every Principled BSDF socket with the image behind it,
the material slot table of every mesh object, and the connected components of Wheel_Pegs;
then parse the GLB's JSON chunk for the audit counts, the camera, the punctual lights and
each material's factors, textures and alphaMode; then write both into this file. Never
call bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile. striker_lever_arm and clearance_deflection_deg are the
only two numbers here that this pass did not re-derive; the flapper notes say so.
COORDINATE SYSTEM: option A of docs/export_notes.md section 4. Every vector at the top
level of this file is in the exported glTF +Y-up frame, the same frame as the geometry in
assets/wheel_stage.glb. World up is (0, 1, 0). No rotation is applied at load.
The Blender Z-up source values are kept beside each entry under a 'blender' object, for
cross-checking against docs/agent_plan.md and docs/scene_audit.md, which are Z-up.
The map the exporter used is (x, y, z)_blender -> (x, z, -y)_gltf, a proper rotation.
Every array of objects has the same keys in every element, so plain serde structs with no
Option and no #[serde(default)] deserialise this file.
generated_by: cleanup pass, regenerated from wheel_stage.blend and assets/wheel_stage.glb

camera.name: Cam_Hero
notes: fov_y_deg is derived from the 22 mm lens on the 36 mm HORIZONTAL sensor at 1672x941:
Do not use Blender's camera.angle_y, recorded under blender.angle_y_rad; sensor_fit
is HORIZONTAL, so the 36 mm sensor spans the width and angle_y is the wrong fit.
glb_yfov_rad is what the exporter wrote into the GLB and agrees with fov_y_rad.
target is the point on the camera axis closest to Wheel_Root, so look_at(position,
target, up=(0,1,0)) reproduces Cam_Hero's framing exactly. Use it for --shot.
To keep the horizontal framing when the window resizes, recompute fov_y from fov_x_rad
and the live viewport aspect.

lighting_notes: energy_watts is Blender radiant power. three-d's intensity is a dimensionless multiplier,
so convert; src/lighting.rs owns the conversion and records it in docs/api/lighting.md.
exported_candela is what the GLB holds for the two spots after the exporter's conversion.
It is recorded for traceability only. Never feed it to three-d.
in_glb is false for the four AREA lights: KHR_lights_punctual has no area light, so the
exporter wrote their nodes without light data. This file is the only source for all six.
direction is the way the light points, already normalised, in the glTF frame. Blender and
glTF punctual lights both emit down local -Z, so this needs no further sign flip.
All four AREA lights are SQUARE, so size is the full edge length in metres and Blender's
size_y is unused. three-d has no area light either: treat them as directional or point
casts_shadow is true on all six in the .blend. three-d takes one shadow map per light,
so which ones actually get one is src/lighting.rs's decision.
Any lamp the renderer adds that is not in this list stands in for emissive geometry that
casts no light in three-d. Emissive geometry that really is emissive in the .blend may be
stood in for by a lamp; MAT_Bulb_Glass on Wheel_Bulbs is the one case, at emission
strength 3.0. Such a lamp must be documented as a stand-in wherever it is described.
material_notes: 19 materials, not the 20 in docs/agent_plan.md. MAT_Rubber_Black is not in the .blend and
not in the GLB. Do not create it.
Every value here was read out of the .blend's Principled BSDF in this pass. The five
fields the renderer applies - base_color, metallic, roughness, alpha, effective_emission -
are the .blend's own, with no look-dev deviation of any kind. A constant in Rust that
duplicates one of them is a defect even when the two agree, because they will drift.
base_color and emission_color are linear RGB. three-d's PhysicalMaterial::albedo is
sRGB-encoded, so encode before assigning.
effective_emission is emission_color * emission_strength, the radiance the Blender shader
emits, and it is the value to use for a material with no emission texture.
alpha_mode is what the GLB declares. MAT_Crystal is the only BLEND, at alpha 0.55; every
other material is OPAQUE. Blender 5's material.blend_method reads HASHED on all 19 and is
not a useful signal.
base_color_texture, emission_texture and uv_map name the image that drives a socket in
the .blend, empty when a socket holds a flat colour. MAT_LED_Screen is the only textured
material: T_LEDWall_Sky feeds both its Base Color and its Emission Color through a UV Map
node reading UVMap. Its base_color and emission_color (0.35, 0.3, 0.6) are the socket
defaults behind the texture, so they are the fallback and not the picture; the GLB drops
them and writes baseColorFactor (1, 1, 1, 1) instead. Never write a flat colour over an
image: the shader multiplies the two.
used_by lists every object and slot that carries the material, straight from the .blend.
Use it instead of hardcoding a node name. Note MAT_Metal_Polished carries Wheel_Hub, so
the hub is polished metal at metallic 1.0 and roughness 0.14 like Wheel_Axle beside it.
The glb_* fields record what assets/wheel_stage.glb carries, for traceability.
glb_base_color_factor, glb_metallic and glb_roughness are equal to the .blend's own
base_color, metallic and roughness for all 19 materials, so glTF transport loses none of
the three. What it does lose is emission: the exporter normalises the emissive factor to
a maximum of 1 and puts the rest into KHR_materials_emissive_strength, which
three-d-asset 0.10 ignores, so an importer sees only the factor and every glow arrives
too dim. Re-apply effective_emission. PhysicalMaterial::albedo is also four u8s, so an
imported albedo is quantised and a linear value under about 0.01 loses a digit.
A per-node override of a material value is only honest when it restores something
transport lost. On the evidence of the three glb_* fields, that is nothing but emission.

notes: The author's own T_LEDWall_Sky drives both Base Color and Emission Color of
MAT_LED_Screen through a UV Map node reading UVMap, and the fixed export carries it:
the GLB holds 1 image and 2 textures, and MAT_LED_Screen has a baseColorTexture and
an emissiveTexture with KHR_materials_emissive_strength 1.5.
So the texture is the primary path. Show it as the mesh's own UVMap addresses it, with
no re-windowing, no magnification and no per-side grade: none of that is in the .blend.
A procedural sky may stay behind a named constant as a fallback, which is the standing
instruction in docs/agent_plan.md, but it is not what the scene says.
The material is on two objects, Wall_Screen and slot 0 of Podium_Riser, so bind any
screen-specific treatment by object or primitive and never by material name alone.
Wheel_Root is a mesh-less node with identity rotation and unit scale, so one rotation on
it moves its 56 children and nothing else.
In the glTF frame the wheel disc lies in the XY plane and spins about Z. A rotation of
phi about Blender +Y equals Rz(-phi) in glTF. Positive phi is clockwise from the hero
camera in both frames.
Sector nn is centred at theta = (nn-1)*7.5 deg, measured in the Blender wheel-local
frame as atan2(x_local, z_local), so sector 1 points straight up at rotation 0.
Pegs sit on the sector boundaries: theta_k = 3.75 + k*7.5 deg, k = 0..47. Re-measured
for this manifest from Wheel_Pegs by walking its connected components: 96 islands, 48
peg bodies of 146 vertices each whose centres are all at radius 2.245 m and which span
radius 2.189 to 2.301 m, plus 48 studs of 14 vertices at radius 2.13 m.
peg_stud_size is the radial span of a peg body, peg_outer_radius minus
peg_inner_radius, measured to 0.11199034 m. The manifest this pass replaced said
0.112, which is the same span computed from endpoints already rounded to three
decimals. src/spin.rs's geometry_comes_from_the_manifest asserts its stud window
against a hardcoded 0.112 / 2.245 and now fails by 4.3e-6: it should read both
numbers from here, which is the whole point of this file.
idle_rate_rad_per_s is a look-dev choice, not a measurement. src/spin.rs owns it.
The blade hangs along object-local -Z from its hinge and deflects about the same axis the
wheel spins about, so the same sign rule applies to psi.
blade_length is the hinge-to-tip distance, -local_min[2] of the object's bound box.
striker_lever_arm and clearance_deflection_deg are CARRIED FORWARD from the earlier
measurement of the striker tab island; this pass re-derived every other number here
from the .blend but not those two. The striker tab clears the peg tips at psi =
+/-32.2 deg; that is the upper bound on a tick amplitude, not a target. Tab and peg
never intersect at rest, so the tick has to be driven kinematically from the wheel angle.
One peg passes the top every 7.5 deg of wheel rotation, so the tick rate is 48 times the
spin rate in revolutions per second.

crop_notes: Pixel rectangles at 1672x941, the resolution of both docs/wheel_stage.png and --shot.
x,y is the top-left corner and y grows downward.
src/shot.rs reads these six rectangles from this file. It holds no copy of them.
serde_hint: The struct shape in src/manifest.rs that deserialises this file, with no Option and no
#[serde(default)] anywhere. Every prose array - doc, notes, lighting_notes,
material_notes, crop_notes, serde_hint - is an unknown key to serde and is skipped, so
editing a note never breaks the load.
Manifest { generated_by, source_blend, blender_version, glb, scene_name,
up_axis: UpAxis, vectors_in: VectorFrame, render: RenderSpec, camera: CameraSpec,
lights: Vec<LightSpec>, materials: Vec<MaterialSpec>, textures: Vec<TextureSpec>,
screen: ScreenSpec, wheel: WheelSpec, flapper: FlapperSpec, crops: Vec<CropRect>,
glb_audit: GlbAudit }
MaterialSpec { name, base_color: [f32;3], metallic, roughness, alpha, alpha_mode,
emission_strength, emission_color: [f32;3], effective_emission: [f32;3],
base_color_texture, emission_texture, uv_map, used_by: Vec<MaterialUse>,
glb_base_color_factor: [f32;4], glb_metallic, glb_roughness, glb_alpha_mode,
glb_emissive_factor: [f32;3], glb_emissive_strength,
glb_has_base_color_texture: bool, glb_has_emissive_texture: bool }
MaterialUse { node, slot }
LightSpec { name, kind (rename from "type"), position, direction, color,
energy_watts, size, shape, spot_size_rad, spot_blend, cone_outer_half_angle_rad,
cone_inner_half_angle_rad, casts_shadow, in_glb, exported_candela,
blender: LightBlender }
TextureSpec { name, source_png, width, height, colorspace, mime_type,
embedded_in_glb, glb_texture_indices: Vec<u32>, wrap, interpolation, uv_map }
ScreenSpec { node, material, texture, uv_map, emission_strength, in_glb,
also_on: Vec<String> }
CropRect { name, x, y, w, h, checks }
"type" is a Rust keyword, so the light kind needs #[serde(rename = "type")].
up_axis is the string "Y" and describes the geometry in the GLB. It does NOT mean a
conversion is still owed: the vectors in this file are already in that frame. Do not
apply Blender-to-glTF mapping to any top-level vector here.

notes: Measured by parsing assets/wheel_stage.glb for this manifest; tools/validate_export.py
asserts the same numbers.
primitives is 179: 153 meshes plus 26 extra material slots, and it is the number of
parts src/scene.rs builds.
punctual_lights is 2: only Beam_L and Beam_R survived, because KHR_lights_punctual has
no area light.
images 1 and textures 2: one embedded PNG, T_LEDWall_Sky, referenced twice - once as
MAT_LED_Screen's baseColorTexture and once as its emissiveTexture.
file_bytes is 10654664, 10.16 MiB.
Do not use a GLB checksum as a build fingerprint: two runs of the export differ in 45
TEXCOORD_0 float32 values by one ULP, from bevel UV generation.
